title: Barrie Craig
paragraphs: A New York private-eye drama centered on Barrie Craig, a capable independent detective played by William Gargan, who takes on murder, fraud, and other criminal cases.

NBC private-eye drama starring William Gargan as Madison Avenue investigator Barrie Craig. The series was usually sustaining, with occasional sponsors, and shifted production from New York to Hollywood late in the run. The frozen GRH snapshot contains 59 surviving broadcasts rather than the full original run.

GRH documents the program through NBC New York production (October 3, 1951 to 1954) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and NBC Hollywood production (1954 to June 30, 1955) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|william-gargan|William Gargan]] (performer on 59 recordings), Don Pardo (announcer on 31 recordings), John Roeburt (writer on 26 recordings), Himan Brown (director on 21 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Louis Vittes (writer on 18 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Arthur Jacobson (director on 12 recordings), and Edward King (announcer on 8 recordings and director on 1 recording).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include private investigation and detective work, murder, homicide and suspicious death, fraud, theft, blackmail and deception, money, valuables and financial motive, marriage, family and domestic conflict, and show business, media and public spectacle.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar private-eye radio cycle, Sustaining network crime drama, Network production shift from New York to Hollywood, and Crime drama in the late network-radio era.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (50 shared credited people), [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (45 shared credited people), [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (35 shared credited people), [[show|philip-marlowe|The Adventures of Philip Marlowe]] (34 shared credited people), and [[show|escape|Escape]] (32 shared credited people).
